messages.text: Antonelli takes surprise pole to boost chances of sealing title in USA

metadata.summary: Kimi Antonelli beat Max Verstappen to pole position for the United States Grand Prix to boost his chances of sealing a maiden world championship in Sunday's race.
metadata.content: United States GP Qualifying: Kimi Antonelli beats Max Verstappen to surprise pole to boost chances of sealing maiden F1 title on Sunday | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to main content United States GP Qualifying: Kimi Antonelli beats Max Verstappen to surprise pole to boost chances of sealing maiden F1 title on Sunday Kimi Antonelli stuns Max Verstappen to take pole in Austin; Antonelli could be crowned world champion on Sunday if he wins and other results go his way; watch the United States GP live on Sky Sports F1 & Sky Sports Main Event at 8pm on Sunday, with build-up from 6.30pm Sunday 25 October 2026 00:41, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from qualifying for the 2026 United States Grand Prix Kimi Antonelli beat Max Verstappen to pole position for the United States Grand Prix to boost his chances of sealing a maiden world championship in Sunday's race. The 20-year-old Mercedes driver is all but certain to become Formula 1's youngest ever champion but could clinch the title with five rounds to spare if he wins in Austin on Sunday and other placings go his way. It was perhaps the most unlikely of Antonelli's seven poles this season as he came from nowhere in Q3 to surge ahead of Verstappen, who had appeared for most of the weekend to be battling Ferrari for the front-row positions. metadata.summary: Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff believes it is "not realistic" for Kimi Antonelli to win the 2026 F1 Drivers' Championship on Sunday at the United States Grand Prix, despite the Italian starting on pole position.
metadata.content: United States GP: How likely is pole-sitter Kimi Antonelli to win 2026 F1 Drivers' Championship on Sunday in Austin? | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to main content United States GP: How likely is pole-sitter Kimi Antonelli to win 2026 F1 Drivers' Championship on Sunday in Austin? Watch the United States GP live on Sky Sports F1 & Sky Sports Main Event at 8pm on Sunday, with build up from 6.30pm Nigel Chiu Sports Journalist @NigelCJourno Sunday 25 October 2026 07:25, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Craig Slater explains how Kimi Antonelli can clinch the F1 world title at the United States Grand Prix Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff believes it is "not realistic" for Kimi Antonelli to win the 2026 F1 Drivers' Championship on Sunday at the United States Grand Prix, despite the Italian starting on pole position. Antonelli was not expected to claim top spot in qualifying but produced a superb lap in Q3 to beat Red Bull's Max Verstappen and take his first pole since July's Belgian Grand Prix. Should Antonelli win Sunday's race in Austin with Lewis Hamilton finishing fifth or lower and George Russell no better than ninth, he will seal the title with five rounds remaining. messages.text: Littler powers past Aspinall to reach European Championship quarter-finals

metadata.summary: Luke Littler remains on course to win the one major title he's never won as he beat Nathan Aspinall 10-5 in the second round of the European Championship Darts on Saturday evening.
metadata.content: Luke Littler still on course to win European Championship Darts after second-round win over Nathan Aspinall | Darts News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Luke Littler still on course to win European Championship Darts after second-round win over Nathan Aspinall The Nuke secures the second highest three-dart average in the history of the tournament as he powers into quarter-finals; Watch the Grand Slam of Darts in Wolverhampton live on Sky Sports from November 14-22 By Stephen Mills and Raz Mirza Saturday 24 October 2026 22:35, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player See the moment Luke Littler sealed the second-best average in European Championship history Luke Littler remains on course to win the one major title he's never won as he beat Nathan Aspinall 10-5 in the second round of the European Championship Darts on Saturday evening. Littler produced the second-best average in the competition's history - his 114.47 has only ever been bettered by Phil Taylor's 118.14 - as he secured an impressive victory in Dortmund. Aspinall produced ten 180s in the match - three more than his opponent - but it wasn't enough to survive the onslaught from the world No 1, who won the first four legs of the match in 12 darts or fewer. Aspinall briefly rallied to reduce the score to 5-4, but Littler controlled the second half of the game and, despite one brief interruption to deal with a vocal fan in the crowd, he ultimately closed out the match on D10. messages.text: Smith beats Puello in thriller to retain WBC title and stay unbeaten

metadata.summary: Dalton Smith retained his WBC light-welterweight title with a thrilling, split-decision victory over Alberto Puello on Saturday night.
metadata.content: Dalton Smith beats Alberto Puello to retain WBC light-welterweight title after split decision victory | Boxing News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Dalton Smith beats Alberto Puello to retain WBC light-welterweight title after split decision victory Dalton Smith wins on his Sheffield homecoming; the 29-year-old was taken the distance in his first title defence but makes it 20 wins from 20 fights as a professional; two judges score it 115-113 in his favour and one 116-112 to Alberto Puello, who suffers just his second defeat in 27 Saturday 24 October 2026 22:59, UK Image: Dalton Smith succesfully defended his WBC light-welterweight title with a split decision victory over Alberto Puello Dalton Smith retained his WBC light-welterweight title with a thrilling, split-decision victory over Alberto Puello on Saturday night. On his homecoming at Utilita Arena, the Sheffield man was taken the distance in his first title defence, but kept his unbeaten record in tact as judges Kieran McCann of England and Spain's Jon Llona both scored the bout 115-113 in his favour, while Filipino Ray Danseco had it 116-112 to Puello. Puello - is a former WBA and WBC champion - suffered only his second defeat in 27 fights. Smith has won 20 from 20, including beating Subriel Matias in New York in January - who inflicted Puello's only previous loss - to become world champion. metadata.summary: They say bad things come in threes. That was certainly the case for Chelsea on a miserable evening at Stamford Bridge as they lost 2-0 to Tottenham and were described as "awful" by Gary Neville.
metadata.content: Chelsea: Cole Palmer red card, Mike Penders howler and 'out-coached' by Roberto De Zerbi on horror night for Xabi Alonso | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Analysis Chelsea: Cole Palmer red card, Mike Penders howler and 'out-coached' by Roberto De Zerbi on horror night for Xabi Alonso Tottenham won at Stamford Bridge for just the second time in 35 visits in the Premier League; Chelsea created very little in the defeat with Gary Neville calling them 'awful'; Cole Palmer was described as 'petulant' following his red card; Mike Penders made a 'monumental' error Sunday 25 October 2026 07:08, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player FREE TO WATCH: Highlights from the Premier League match between Chelsea and Tottenham Hotspur They say bad things come in threes. That was certainly the case for Chelsea on a miserable evening at Stamford Bridge as they lost 2-0 to Tottenham and were described as "awful" by Gary Neville. Spurs had won only one of their previous 34 Premier League visits to Chelsea but dominated Xabi Alonso's side from start to finish, with an own goal from Mike Penders and a stunning late strike from Mathys Tel securing a well-deserved win for Roberto De Zerbi's side. To add to their woes, on an evening where the dismal weather matched their performance, Cole Palmer was sent off for a second bookable offence after already escaping a straight red card earlier in the game, having barged into Spurs midfielder Mateus Fernandes.
